verses.37:21: And his noble one will be from himself, and his ruler will come forth from his midst; I will bring him near, and he will approach Me, for who is this who would pledge his heart to approach Me? declares the LORD."
verses.37:23: Look, the tempest of the LORD! Fury has gone forth, a sweeping tempest; upon the head of the wicked it will whirl down.
verses.37:24: The burning anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has done and until He has established the purposes of His heart; in the latter days you will understand it.
verses.38:1: "At that time," declares the LORD, "I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they will be a people to Me."
verses.38:2: This is what the LORD says: "The people, survivors of the sword, found favor in the wilderness, as Israel went to find his rest."
verses.38:3: From afar the LORD appeared to me: "With an eternal love I have loved you; therefore I have drawn you with loyal love.
verses.38:4: Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel! Again you will adorn yourself with your tambourines and go out in the dance of those who celebrate.
verses.38:5: Again you will plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters will plant and enjoy the harvest.
verses.38:6: For there will be a day when watchmen call out in the hill country of Ephraim, 'Rise, and let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.'"
verses.38:7: For this is what the LORD says: "Shout joyfully for Jacob with gladness, and cry out for the foremost of the nations; announce it, offer praise, and say, 'Save Your people, LORD, the remnant of Israel!'
verses.38:8: Look, I am bringing them from the northern land, and I will gather them from the farthest reaches of the earth—among them the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labor together; as a great assembly they will return here.
verses.38:9: With weeping they will come, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them; I will guide them to streams of water, on a level path where they will not stumble, for I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is My firstborn."
verses.38:10: Hear the word of the LORD, nations, and announce it in the distant coastlands; say, "He who scattered Israel will gather him and watch over him like a shepherd over his flock."
verses.38:11: For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and has redeemed him from the hand of one mightier than he.
verses.38:12: They will come and shout joyfully on the height of Zion, and they will stream to the goodness of the LORD—for grain, for new wine, and for fresh oil, and for the young of the flock and the herd; their soul will be like a well-watered garden, and they will not languish anymore.
verses.38:13: Then the virgin will be glad in the dance, and the young men and the old together. "I will turn their mourning into joy; I will comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.
verses.38:14: I will saturate the soul of the priests with richness, and My people will be satisfied with My goodness," declares the LORD.
verses.38:15: This is what the LORD says: "A voice is heard in Ramah—wailing, bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping over her children; she refuses to be comforted over her children, because they are gone."
verses.38:16: This is what the LORD says: "Hold back your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your labor," declares the LORD, "and they will return from the land of the enemy.
verses.38:17: And there is hope for your future," declares the LORD, "and children will return to their territory."
verses.38:18: "I have indeed heard Ephraim grieving: 'You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for You are the LORD my God.
verses.38:19: For after I turned, I felt remorse; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed and also humiliated, because I bore the disgrace of my youth.'
verses.38:20: Is Ephraim a precious son to Me? Is he a child of delight? For whenever I speak against him, I certainly remember him still. Therefore My inward parts yearn for him; I will surely show him compassion," declares the LORD.
verses.38:21: Set up road markers for yourself; place guideposts for yourself. Set your heart on the highway, the road you went. Return, virgin Israel; return to these cities of yours.
verses.38:22: How long will you waver back and forth, wayward daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman will surround a man.
verses.38:23: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Once again they will speak this word in the land of Judah and in its cities when I restore their fortunes: 'May the LORD bless you, dwelling of righteousness, holy mountain!'
verses.38:24: And Judah and all its cities will dwell in it together—farmers and those who travel about with the flock.
verses.38:25: For I have refreshed the weary soul, and every languishing soul I have filled."
verses.38:26: Upon this I woke up and looked, and my sleep was sweet to me.
verses.38:27: "Look, days are coming," declares the LORD, "and I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of mankind and the seed of livestock.
verses.38:28: And it will be that just as I kept watch over them to uproot and to tear down, to demolish, to destroy, and to bring harm, so I will keep watch over them to build and to plant," declares the LORD.
verses.38:29: In those days they will no longer say, "Fathers ate unripe grapes, and the teeth of children are set on edge."
verses.38:30: Rather, each one will die for his own iniquity; every person who eats the unripe grapes—his own teeth will be set on edge.
verses.38:31: "Look, days are coming," declares the LORD, "and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
verses.38:32: not like the covenant that I made with their ancestors on the day I grasped their hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt—My covenant that they themselves violated, even though I was a husband to them," declares the LORD.
verses.38:33: "Rather, this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days," declares the LORD: "I will place My law within them, and upon their heart I will inscribe it; I will be God to them, and they will be a people to Me.
verses.38:34: And no longer will each one teach his neighbor, nor each one his brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' for all of them will know Me, from the smallest of them to the greatest of them," declares the LORD, "for I will pardon their iniquity, and their sin I will no longer remember."
verses.38:35: This is what the LORD says: "If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out, then I too will reject all the seed of Israel for everything they have done," declares the LORD.
verses.38:36: This is what the LORD says, who sets the sun for light by day and the statutes of the moon and stars for light by night, who agitates the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of hosts is His name:
verses.38:37: "If these statutes depart from before Me," declares the LORD, "then the seed of Israel will also cease from being a nation before Me for all time."
verses.38:38: "Look, days are coming," declares the LORD, "and the city will be built for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
verses.38:39: The measuring line will go out further straight ahead to the hill of Gareb, and then it will turn toward Goah.
verses.38:40: And the whole valley of the corpses and the ashes, and all the terraced fields as far as the Brook Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will not be uprooted or demolished again forever."
verses.39:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah—that was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.39:2: Now at that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard that was in the house of the king of Judah,
verses.39:3: where Zedekiah, king of Judah, had confined him, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it,
verses.39:4: and Zedekiah, king of Judah, will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he will certainly be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes;
verses.39:5: and he will lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will stay until I visit him, declares the LORD. Even if you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed'?"
verses.39:6: And Jeremiah said, "The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.39:7: 'Look, Hanamel, the son of Shallum your uncle, is coming to you, saying, "Buy for yourself my field that is in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it."'
verses.39:8: Then Hanamel, my uncle's son, came to me at the courtyard of the guard according to the word of the LORD, and he said to me, 'Please buy my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Benjamin, for the right of inheritance is yours, and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself.' Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
verses.39:9: So I bought the field that was in Anathoth from Hanamel, my uncle's son, and I weighed out the silver to him, seventeen shekels of silver.
verses.39:10: I wrote in the deed and sealed it, and called witnesses, and weighed out the silver on scales.
verses.39:11: Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy—the terms and stipulations—and the open copy.
verses.39:12: And I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanamel my uncle, and in the sight of the witnesses who wrote in the deed of purchase, in the sight of all the Jews who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
verses.39:13: And I commanded Baruch in their sight, saying,
verses.39:14: 'This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds—this deed of purchase, the sealed one, and this open deed—and place them in a clay vessel, so that they may endure for many days.
verses.39:15: For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Once more houses, fields, and vineyards will be bought in this land.'
verses.39:16: Then I prayed to the LORD after giving the deed of purchase to Baruch, the son of Neriah, saying,
verses.39:17: 'Ah, Lord GOD! Look, You Yourself made the heavens and the earth by Your great strength and by Your outstretched arm; not a single thing is too difficult for You.
verses.39:18: You show loyal love to thousands, yet repay the iniquity of fathers into the lap of their children after them—the great, mighty God; the LORD of hosts is His name—
verses.39:19: great in counsel and abundant in deed, whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of mankind, to give to each person according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds,
verses.39:20: who set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day both in Israel and among mankind, and made for Yourself a name, as it is this day.
verses.39:21: And You brought Your people Israel out from the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders, with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
verses.39:22: You gave them this land, which You swore to their fathers to give to them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.39:23: They entered and took possession of it, yet they did not listen to Your voice and did not walk in Your law; all that You commanded them to do, they did not do. Therefore You have caused all this disaster to come upon them.
verses.39:24: Look, the siege ramps have come up to the city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword, the famine, and the pestilence. What You spoke has come to pass, and look, You see it.
verses.39:25: Yet You Yourself have said to me, Lord GOD, "Buy the field for yourself with silver and call witnesses," though the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.'"
verses.39:26: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying,
verses.39:27: "Look, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything at all too difficult for Me?
verses.39:28: Therefore this is what the LORD says: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
verses.39:29: And the Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will enter and set this city on fire and burn it, together with the houses on whose rooftops they burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, so as to provoke Me to anger.
verses.39:30: For the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have been doing only evil in My sight from their youth; indeed, the sons of Israel have been doing nothing but provoking Me to anger with the work of their hands," declares the LORD.
verses.39:31: "For this city has been to Me a provocation of My anger and My wrath from the day they built it right up to this day, so that I will remove it from before My face,
verses.39:32: because of all the evil of the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah that they have done to provoke Me to anger—they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets, along with the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.39:33: They turned their back to Me and not their face; and though I taught them, rising early and teaching, yet they would not listen to receive discipline.
verses.39:34: Instead, they set their detestable things in the house over which My name is called, to defile it.
verses.39:35: And they built the high places of Baal that are in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass over to Molech—something I never commanded them, nor did it ever enter My heart that they should do this abomination—so as to cause Judah to sin.
verses.39:36: Now therefore, this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city of which you are saying, 'It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence':
verses.39:37: Look, I am about to gather them from all the lands to which I drove them in My anger, in My wrath, and in great fury; and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.
verses.39:38: And they will be My people, and I Myself will be their God.
verses.39:39: I will give them one heart and one way, so that they may fear Me all the days, for their good and for the good of their children after them.
verses.39:40: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn back from following them to do them good; and I will put the fear of Me into their hearts, so that they will not turn aside from Me.
verses.39:41: And I will delight over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all My heart and with all My soul.
verses.39:42: For this is what the LORD says: Just as I have brought all this great disaster upon this people, so I am bringing upon them all the good that I am declaring concerning them.
verses.39:43: Fields will be bought in this land of which you are saying, 'It is a desolation, without human or animal; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.'
verses.39:44: People will buy fields with silver, and write in deeds, and seal them, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, in the surroundings of Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the Negev; for I will restore their fortunes," declares the LORD.
verses.40:1: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still detained in the courtyard of the guard, saying,
verses.40:2: "This is what the LORD says who made it, the LORD who forms it to establish it—the LORD is His name:
verses.40:3: Call to Me, and I will answer you, and I will declare to you great and inaccessible things that you have not known.
verses.40:4: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down against the siege ramps and against the sword:
verses.40:5: They are coming to fight against the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of the people whom I have struck down in My anger and in My wrath, for I have hidden My face from this city because of all their wickedness.
verses.40:6: Look, I will bring to it recovery and healing, and I will heal them; and I will reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth.
verses.40:7: And I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and I will rebuild them as at the first.
verses.40:8: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they sinned against Me, and I will forgive all their iniquities by which they sinned against Me and by which they rebelled against Me.
verses.40:9: And it will be to Me a name of joy, a praise, and a splendor before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good that I am doing for them; and they will fear and tremble because of all the good and because of all the peace that I am providing for it."
verses.40:10: This is what the LORD says: "In this place of which you are saying, 'It is a waste, without human and without animal'—in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without human and without inhabitant and without animal—there will once more be heard
verses.40:11: the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the bridegroom and the sound of the bride, the sound of those saying, 'Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good, for His loyal love is forever,' as they bring a thank offering to the house of the LORD. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at the first," says the LORD.
verses.40:12: This is what the LORD of hosts says: "In this place that is a waste, without human or even animal, and in all its cities, there will once more be a pasture for shepherds making flocks lie down.
verses.40:13: In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, in the cities of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, in the surroundings of Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, flocks will once more pass under the hands of the one who counts them," says the LORD.
verses.41:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth under the dominion of his hand, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:
verses.41:2: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
verses.41:3: And you will not escape from his hand, for you will surely be captured and given into his hand; and your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and you will go to Babylon.
verses.41:4: Yet hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah! This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword.
verses.41:5: In peace you will die; and as with the burnings for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will make a burning for you, and they will lament for you, "Alas, lord!" For I Myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.'"
verses.41:6: Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.
verses.41:7: Now the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the remaining cities of Judah, against Lachish and against Azekah, for these remained among the cities of Judah as fortified cities.
verses.41:8: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people who were in Jerusalem to proclaim release to them,
verses.41:9: that each man should let his male slave and each man his female slave, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, go free, so that no one should hold them in bondage—a Judean, his brother.
verses.41:10: And all the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant obeyed, that each man should let his male slave and each man his female slave go free, so as not to hold them in bondage any longer; they obeyed and let them go.
verses.41:11: Yet afterward they turned back and brought back the male slaves and the female slaves whom they had let go free, and subdued them to be male slaves and female slaves.
verses.41:12: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
verses.41:13: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "I Myself made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slaves, saying,
verses.41:14: 'At the end of seven years each of you shall let go his Hebrew brother who has been sold to you and has served you six years; you shall let him go free from you.' But your fathers did not listen to Me, nor did they incline their ear.
verses.41:15: And you turned today and did what is right in My eyes, proclaiming release, each man to his neighbor; and you made a covenant before Me in the house upon which My name is called.
verses.41:16: Then you turned back and profaned My name, and you brought back, each man his male slave and each man his female slave, whom you had let go free according to their own desire, and you subdued them to be male slaves and female slaves for you."
verses.41:17: Therefore this is what the LORD says: "You have not listened to Me to proclaim release, each man to his brother and each man to his neighbor. Look, I am proclaiming a release for you," declares the LORD, "to the sword, to the plague, and to the famine; and I will make you an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
verses.41:18: And I will make the men who have transgressed My covenant, who have not upheld the words of the covenant that they made before Me, like the calf that they cut in two and passed between its parts—
verses.41:19: the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the eunuchs and the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf—
verses.41:20: I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life; and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and for the beasts of the earth.
verses.41:21: And I will give Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which is withdrawing from you.
verses.41:22: Look, I am commanding," declares the LORD, "and I will bring them back to this city; and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without an inhabitant."
verses.42:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
verses.42:2: "Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them, and bring them into the house of the LORD, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink."
verses.42:3: So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.
verses.42:4: And I brought them into the house of the LORD, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, which was beside the chamber of the officials, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
verses.42:5: Then I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pitchers full of wine and cups, and I said to them, "Drink wine."
verses.42:6: But they said, "We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, 'You shall not drink wine, you or your sons, forever.
verses.42:7: You shall not build a house, nor sow seed, nor plant a vineyard, nor shall you have any; rather, you shall dwell in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the land where you sojourn.'
verses.42:8: And we have obeyed the voice of Jehonadab son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, not to drink wine all our days—we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters—
verses.42:9: and not to build houses for us to dwell in; nor do we have a vineyard or field or seed.
verses.42:10: We have dwelt in tents, and we have obeyed and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
verses.42:11: But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, 'Come, and let us go into Jerusalem away from the army of the Chaldeans and away from the army of Aram.' So we have dwelt in Jerusalem."
verses.42:12: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:
verses.42:13: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Go and say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, 'Will you not receive instruction to listen to My words?' declares the LORD.
verses.42:14: 'The words of Jehonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons not to drink wine, have been upheld; and they have not drunk to this day, for they obeyed the command of their father. Yet I Myself have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not listened to Me.
verses.42:15: And I sent to you all My servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying, "Turn back now, each man from his evil way, and make your deeds good, and do not go after other gods to serve them; then you will dwell in the land that I gave to you and to your fathers." Yet you did not incline your ear, nor did you listen to Me.
verses.42:16: Indeed, the sons of Jehonadab son of Rechab have upheld the command of their father that he commanded them, but this people has not listened to Me.'"
verses.42:17: Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I am bringing upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have spoken against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, and I called to them and they did not answer."
verses.42:18: Then Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Because you have obeyed the command of Jehonadab your father, and kept all his commands, and done according to all that he commanded you,
verses.42:19: therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: A man to stand before Me shall not be cut off from Jonadab son of Rechab all the days.'"
verses.43:1: Now it happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
verses.43:2: "Take for yourself a book scroll, and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you about Israel, about Judah, and about all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah up to this day.
verses.43:3: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the calamity that I am planning to do to them, so that they may turn back, each one from his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin."
verses.43:4: Then Jeremiah called Baruch, son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a book scroll, from the mouth of Jeremiah, all the words of the LORD that He had spoken to him.
verses.43:5: Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, "I am restrained; I cannot enter the house of the LORD.
verses.43:6: So you yourself go and read the words of the LORD from the scroll that you wrote from my mouth, in the hearing of the people at the house of the LORD on a fast day; and you shall also read them in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities.
verses.43:7: Perhaps their supplication will be laid before the LORD, and they will turn back, each one from his evil way; for great are the anger and the fury that the LORD has spoken against this people."
verses.43:8: So Baruch, son of Neriah, did according to everything Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, reading from the book the words of the LORD at the house of the LORD.
verses.43:9: Now it happened in the fifth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, that all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who had come from the cities of Judah into Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the LORD.
verses.43:10: Then Baruch read the words of Jeremiah from the book at the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah, son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
verses.43:11: Now Micaiah, son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the book.
verses.43:12: He went down to the king's house, to the scribe's chamber, and look, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
verses.43:13: Micaiah reported to them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the book in the hearing of the people.
verses.43:14: Then all the officials sent Jehudi, son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, "The scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people—take it in your hand and come." So Baruch, son of Neriah, took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
verses.43:15: They said to him, "Please sit down and read it in our hearing." So Baruch read in their hearing.
verses.43:16: When they heard all the words, they turned in dread, each toward his companion, and said to Baruch, "We must certainly report all these words to the king."
verses.43:17: Then they questioned Baruch, saying, "Please tell us, how did you write all these words from his mouth?"
verses.43:18: And Baruch said to them, "From his mouth he would recite all these words to me, while I was writing them in the book with ink."
verses.43:19: So the officials said to Baruch, "Go, conceal yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are."
verses.43:20: Then they went to the king in the courtyard—having deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe—and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king.
verses.43:21: The king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. Then Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the officials who stood beside the king.
verses.43:22: Now the king was seated in the winter house in the ninth month, and the brazier was burning before him.
verses.43:23: And whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut it with a scribe's knife and throw it into the fire that was in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire that was on the brazier.
verses.43:24: Yet they felt no dread and did not tear their garments—neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words.
verses.43:25: Indeed, Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah appealed to the king not to burn the scroll, yet he did not listen to them.
verses.43:26: Then the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the LORD concealed them.
verses.43:27: Now the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
verses.43:28: "Once more, take for yourself another scroll and write on it all the earlier words that were on the first scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
verses.43:29: And about Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, 'This is what the LORD says: You yourself burned this scroll, saying, "Why did you write on it, saying that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land, and eliminate human and animal from it?"
verses.43:30: Therefore this is what the LORD says regarding Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one sitting on the throne of David, and his corpse shall be thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.
verses.43:31: And I will call him, his seed, and his servants to account for their iniquity, and I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah all the calamity that I spoke against them, yet they did not listen.'"
verses.43:32: So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch, son of Neriah, the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and even more—many words like them—were added to them.
verses.44:1: Now Zedekiah, son of Josiah—whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made king in the land of Judah—reigned as king in place of Coniah, son of Jehoiakim.
verses.44:2: Yet neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that He spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.44:3: Now King Zedekiah sent Jehucal, son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah, son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "Please pray on our behalf to the LORD our God."
verses.44:4: Meanwhile, Jeremiah was coming in and going out among the people, for they had not placed him in the prison.
verses.44:5: And Pharaoh's army had marched out from Egypt; when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.44:6: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
verses.44:7: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah, who sent you to Me to inquire of Me, 'Look, Pharaoh's army, which has marched out to aid you, is returning to its own land, Egypt.
verses.44:8: And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city; they will capture it and burn it with fire.'
verses.44:9: This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, 'The Chaldeans will surely depart from us,' for they will not depart.
verses.44:10: For even if you struck down the entire army of Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and wounded men were left among them, they would still rise up, each man in his tent, and burn this city with fire."
verses.44:11: Now it happened, when the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
verses.44:12: that Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to obtain a share from there among the people.
verses.44:13: When he was at the Benjamin Gate, an officer of the guard was there whose name was Irijah, son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are defecting to the Chaldeans!"
verses.44:14: Jeremiah said, "A lie! I am not defecting to the Chaldeans." Yet he would not listen to him; so Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
verses.44:15: The officials were enraged with Jeremiah, and they beat him and placed him in the house of imprisonment, the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into the prison.
verses.44:16: Thus Jeremiah entered the dungeon and the vaulted cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.
verses.44:17: Then King Zedekiah sent and had him brought, and the king questioned him in secret in his house and said, "Is there a word from the LORD?" Jeremiah said, "There is." And he said, "Into the hand of the king of Babylon you will be given."
verses.44:18: And Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "In what way have I sinned against you, against your servants, or against this people, that you have placed me in the prison?
verses.44:19: And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
verses.44:20: And now, please listen, my lord the king; please let my supplication be laid before you, and do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I do not die there."
verses.44:21: Then King Zedekiah commanded, and they consigned Jeremiah to the courtyard of the guard, giving him a loaf of bread each day from the street of the bakers until all the bread was exhausted from the city. Thus Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
verses.45:1: Now Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying,
verses.45:2: "This is what the LORD says: 'Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; his own life will be his as plunder, and he will live.'
verses.45:3: This is what the LORD says: 'This city will certainly be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.'"
verses.45:4: Then the officials said to the king, "Please let this man be put to death, because he is weakening the hands of the men of war who remain in this city and the hands of all the people by speaking words like these to them; for this man is not seeking welfare for this people, but rather harm."
verses.45:5: And King Zedekiah said, "Look, he is in your hand; for the king cannot do anything against you."
verses.45:6: So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchijah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard, and they let Jeremiah down with ropes. Now in the cistern there was no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
verses.45:7: Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a eunuch who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
verses.45:8: So Ebed-melech went out from the king's house and spoke to the king, saying,
verses.45:9: "My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the cistern, and he will die right where he is because of the famine, for there is no more bread in the city."
verses.45:10: Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying, "Take thirty men from here with you, and bring Jeremiah the prophet up from the cistern before he dies."
verses.45:11: So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went into the king's house beneath the treasury, and took from there worn-out rags and worn-out garments, and let them down with ropes to Jeremiah into the cistern.
verses.45:12: Then Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Please put the worn-out rags and garments under your armpits beneath the ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
verses.45:13: So they pulled Jeremiah with the ropes and brought him up from the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
verses.45:14: Then King Zedekiah sent and brought Jeremiah the prophet to himself at the third entrance that is in the house of the LORD. And the king said to Jeremiah, "I am asking you something; do not hide anything from me."
verses.45:15: Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not certainly put me to death? And if I advise you, you will not listen to me."
verses.45:16: So King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in secret, saying, "As the LORD lives, who made this life for us, I will not put you to death, nor will I give you into the hand of these men who are seeking your life."
verses.45:17: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you will indeed go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, then your soul will live, and this city will not be burned with fire, and you and your household will live.
verses.45:18: But if you do not go out to the officials of the king of Babylon, then this city will be given into the hand of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will not escape from their hand.'"
verses.45:19: Then King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Judeans who have defected to the Chaldeans, that they might give me into their hand and abuse me."
verses.45:20: But Jeremiah said, "They will not give you over. Please obey the voice of the LORD in what I am speaking to you, so that it may go well with you and your soul may live.
verses.45:21: But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that the LORD has shown me:
verses.45:22: Look, all the women who remain in the house of the king of Judah are being brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they are saying, 'Your trusted friends have misled you and prevailed over you; your feet have been sunk in the mire; they have turned back.'
verses.45:23: And they are bringing out all your wives and your sons to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape from their hand, for you will be seized by the hand of the king of Babylon, and you will burn this city with fire."
verses.45:24: Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know about these words, and you will not die.
verses.45:25: And if the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Please tell us what you spoke to the king—do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death—and what the king spoke to you,'
verses.45:26: then you shall say to them, 'I was presenting my plea before the king, that he would not send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
verses.45:27: Then all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded. So they stopped speaking with him, for the matter had not been overheard.
verses.45:28: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day that Jerusalem was captured. And so it was when Jerusalem was captured.
verses.46:1: In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem and besieged it.
verses.46:2: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was breached.
verses.46:3: Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came in and sat at the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.
verses.46:14: And they sent and took Jeremiah from the courtyard of the guard, and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to bring him home. So he remained among the people.
verses.46:15: Now the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah while he was confined in the courtyard of the guard, saying,
verses.46:16: "Go and speak to Ebed-melech the Cushite, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing My words against this city for harm and not for good, and they will come about before you on that day.
verses.46:17: But I will deliver you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be given into the hand of the men whom you dread.
verses.46:18: For I will certainly rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword; instead, your life will be yours as plunder, because you have trusted in Me, declares the LORD.'"
verses.47:1: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him while he was bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being exiled to Babylon.
verses.47:2: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place,
verses.47:3: and the LORD has brought it about and done just as He spoke. Because you sinned against the LORD and did not obey His voice, this thing has happened to you.
verses.47:4: And now, look, I am freeing you today from the chains that are on your hands. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will watch over you; but if it is bad in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, refrain. See, the whole land is before you; wherever it is good and right in your eyes to go, go there."
verses.47:5: While he had not yet turned back, he said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people; or go wherever it is right in your eyes to go." Then the captain of the guard gave him provisions and a gift, and let him go.
verses.47:6: So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and stayed with him among the people who remained in the land.
verses.47:7: Now all the commanders of the forces who were in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had entrusted to him men, women, and children, along with some of the poorest of the land, from those who had not been exiled to Babylon.
verses.47:8: So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.47:9: Then Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and to their men, saying, "Do not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.
verses.47:10: As for me, look, I am staying at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us; but as for you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, and put them in your vessels, and live in your cities that you have taken."
verses.47:11: Likewise all the Judeans who were in Moab and among the sons of Ammon and in Edom, and who were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant for Judah and that he had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
verses.47:12: Then all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they gathered wine and summer fruit in very great abundance.
verses.47:13: Now Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were in the field came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
verses.47:14: And they said to him, "Do you indeed know that Baalis king of the sons of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike you dead?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.
verses.47:15: Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah, saying, "Please let me go and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike you dead, so that all Judah who are gathered to you would be scattered, and the remnant of Judah would perish?"
verses.47:16: But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking a lie about Ishmael."
verses.48:1: Now it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, from the royal seed and the chief officers of the king, and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread together there in Mizpah.
verses.48:2: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and he put him to death, the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.48:3: Ishmael also struck down all the Judeans who were with him, with Gedaliah, in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war.
verses.48:4: Now it happened on the second day after Gedaliah was put to death, when no one knew,
verses.48:5: that men came from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria—eighty men—with their beards shaved and their garments torn, and having gashed themselves, with grain offering and frankincense in their hands to bring to the house of the LORD.
verses.48:6: And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping continuously as he walked. When he encountered them, he said to them, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
verses.48:7: And when they came into the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them into the middle of the cistern, he and the men who were with him.
verses.48:8: But ten men were found among them, and they said to Ishmael, "Do not put us to death, for we have hidden stores in the field—wheat and barley and oil and honey." So he held back and did not put them to death among their brothers.
verses.48:9: Now the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down on account of Gedaliah was the one that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with those who were killed.
verses.48:10: Then Ishmael took captive all the remnant of the people who were in Mizpah, the king's daughters and all the people remaining in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:11: Now Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him heard about all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
verses.48:12: So they took all the men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him at the great waters that are in Gibeon.
verses.48:13: And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, they rejoiced.
verses.48:14: So all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around, and they turned back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.
verses.48:15: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the sons of Ammon.
verses.48:16: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him took all the remnant of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam—men, men of war, women, children, and eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
verses.48:17: And they set out and stayed at Geruth Chimham, which is beside Bethlehem, intending to go on to enter Egypt,
verses.48:18: because of the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.49:1: Then all the commanders of the forces, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest drew near.
verses.49:2: And they said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Please let our petition fall before you, and pray on our behalf to the LORD your God, on behalf of all this remnant; for we remain only a few out of many, just as your eyes see us.
verses.49:3: And may the LORD your God tell us the way in which we should walk and the thing that we should do."
verses.49:4: Then Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard. Look, I am going to pray to the LORD your God according to your words, and every word that the LORD answers you I will tell you; I will not withhold a word from you."
verses.49:5: And they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word with which the LORD your God sends you to us.
verses.49:6: Whether good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."
verses.49:7: Now at the end of ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
verses.49:8: Then he summoned Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest.
verses.49:9: And he said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, to whom you sent me to let your petition fall before Him:
verses.49:10: 'If you will indeed stay in this land, then I will build you up and not tear down, and I will plant you and not uproot; for I have relented concerning the disaster that I have done to you.
verses.49:11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid of him,' declares the LORD, 'for I am with you to save you and to rescue you from his hand.
verses.49:12: And I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and bring you back to your own soil.'
verses.49:13: But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' so as not to obey the voice of the LORD your God,
verses.49:14: saying, 'No, rather we will enter the land of Egypt, where we will not see war, nor hear the sound of a trumpet, nor go hungry for bread, and there we will stay,'
verses.49:15: then now therefore hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'If you indeed set your faces to enter Egypt and go to reside there,
verses.49:16: then the sword of which you are afraid will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine about which you are anxious will cling closely after you there in Egypt, and there you will die.
verses.49:17: So it will be with all the men who set their faces to enter Egypt to reside there: they will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence; and they will have no survivor or escapee from the disaster that I am bringing upon them.'
verses.49:18: For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Just as My anger and My wrath were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so My wrath will be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt. And you will become an execration, a horror, a curse, and a reproach, and you will never see this place again.'
verses.49:19: The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: 'Do not enter Egypt!' Know for certain that I have solemnly warned you today.
verses.49:20: For you have practiced deceit at the cost of your own lives, since you yourselves sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray on our behalf to the LORD our God, and according to everything that the LORD our God says, so tell us and we will do it.'
verses.49:21: And I have told you today, yet you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God or anything for which He has sent me to you.
verses.49:22: And now know for certain that you will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence in the place where you desire to go to reside."
verses.50:1: Now when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God, with which the LORD their God had sent him to them, even all these words,
verses.50:2: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men spoke, saying to Jeremiah, "You are speaking falsehood! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'You must not enter Egypt to reside there.'
verses.50:3: Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us in order to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to put us to death and to exile us to Babylon."
verses.50:4: So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces, and all the people did not obey the voice of the LORD to stay in the land of Judah.
verses.50:5: Rather, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations to which they had been driven, to reside in the land of Judah—
verses.50:6: the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
verses.50:7: And they entered the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the LORD; and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
verses.50:8: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.50:9: "Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the mortar in the brick pavement that is at the entrance of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, in the sight of Judean men.
verses.50:10: And say to them, 'This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am sending and will fetch Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
verses.50:11: And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: whoever is for death, to death; whoever is for captivity, to captivity; and whoever is for the sword, to the sword.
verses.50:12: And I will kindle a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive; and he will wrap himself in the land of Egypt just as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.
verses.50:13: And he will shatter the pillars of Beth-shemesh, which is in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the gods of Egypt with fire.'"
verses.51:1: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans who were living in the land of Egypt, those living at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Noph, and in the land of Pathros, saying:
verses.51:2: "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah; look, they are a ruin this day, and no one lives in them,
verses.51:3: because of their evil that they committed to provoke Me to anger, going to burn incense, to serve other gods whom neither they, nor you, nor your fathers had known.
verses.51:4: Yet I sent to you all My servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying, "Please do not commit this abominable thing that I hate."
verses.51:5: But they did not listen nor incline their ear to turn back from their evil, so as not to burn incense to other gods.
verses.51:6: So My wrath and My anger poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin, a desolation, as they are this day.'
verses.51:7: And now, this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Why are you doing great harm against your own lives, to cut off from yourselves man and woman, child and nursing infant, from the midst of Judah, so as not to leave yourselves a remnant,
verses.51:8: provoking Me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to sojourn, in order to cut yourselves off and so that you may become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.51:9: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, the evils of the kings of Judah, the evils of their wives, your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.51:10: They have not been humbled to this day, nor have they feared, nor have they walked in My law and in My statutes that I set before you and before your fathers.'
verses.51:11: Therefore, this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: 'Look, I am setting My face against you for disaster, and to cut off all Judah.
verses.51:12: And I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they will all be consumed; in the land of Egypt they will fall, by the sword and by famine they will be consumed. From the least to the greatest, by the sword and by famine they will die, and they will become an execration, a horror, a curse, and a reproach.
verses.51:13: And I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem, with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence.
verses.51:14: And there will be no fugitive or survivor for the remnant of Judah who have come to sojourn there in the land of Egypt, so as to return to the land of Judah, to which they are lifting up their soul to return to live there; for they will not return, except fugitives.'"
verses.51:15: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing by, a great assembly, and all the people living in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
verses.51:16: "As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you.
verses.51:17: Instead, we will surely carry out every word that has gone out from our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her, just as we ourselves did, we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we were satisfied with bread, and we fared well, and we saw no disaster.
verses.51:18: But from the time we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and by the sword and by famine we have been consumed.
verses.51:19: And when we were burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, was it apart from our husbands that we made cakes for her to form her image and poured out drink offerings to her?"
verses.51:20: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men, to the women, and to all the people who had given him an answer, saying:
verses.51:21: "As for the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your officials, and the people of the land, did not the LORD remember them, and did it not come to His mind?
verses.51:22: So the LORD could no longer bear it, because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations that you committed; therefore your land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, without an inhabitant, as it is this day.
verses.51:23: Because you burned incense and because you sinned against the LORD, and did not obey the voice of the LORD nor walk in His law, in His statutes, and in His testimonies, therefore this disaster has come upon you, as it is this day."
verses.51:24: Then Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, "Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
verses.51:25: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, has spoken, saying: 'You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and have fulfilled it with your hands, saying, "We will surely carry out our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her." Surely confirm your vows, and surely carry out your vows!'
verses.51:26: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt: 'Look, I have sworn by My great name,' says the LORD, 'that My name shall no longer be pronounced by the mouth of any man of Judah, saying, "As the Lord GOD lives," in all the land of Egypt.
verses.51:27: Look, I am watching over them for disaster and not for good, and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by the sword and by famine until they come to an end.
verses.51:28: Yet fugitives from the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to sojourn there will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs.
verses.51:29: And this will be the sign to you,' declares the LORD, 'that I am going to punish you in this place, so that you may know that My words will surely stand against you for disaster.'
verses.51:30: This is what the LORD says: 'Look, I am giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and the one who sought his life.'"
verses.51:31: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
verses.51:32: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
verses.51:33: 'You have said, "Woe to me now, for the LORD has added grief to my pain; I am worn out from my groaning, and I have not found rest."'
verses.51:34: Thus you shall say to him: 'This is what the LORD says: "Look, what I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting, and indeed it is the entire land.
verses.51:35: And as for you, are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them! For look, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh," declares the LORD, "yet I will give you your life as plunder in all the places where you go."'"
verses.52:1: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.52:4: Now it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and they encamped against it and built a siege wall against it all around.
verses.52:5: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.52:6: In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.52:7: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls that was beside the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city, and they went by the way of the Arabah.
verses.52:8: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
verses.52:9: Then they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
verses.52:10: The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
verses.52:11: Then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with bronze fetters, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the house of custody until the day of his death.
verses.52:12: Now in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, came into Jerusalem.
verses.52:13: And he burned the house of the LORD, the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he burned with fire.
verses.52:14: And all the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down all the walls of Jerusalem all around.
verses.52:16: But some of the poorest of the land Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard left behind as vinedressers and as plowmen.
verses.52:17: Now the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that belonged to the house of the LORD, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the LORD, and they carried all their bronze to Babylon.
verses.52:18: And they took the pots, the shovels, the wick trimmers, the basins, the ladles, and all the bronze vessels with which they used to minister.
verses.52:19: And the captain of the guard took the bowls, the firepans, the basins, the pots, the lampstands, the ladles, and the pitchers, what was of gold as gold, and what was of silver as silver.
verses.52:20: As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze oxen that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, there was no weighing the bronze of all these vessels.
verses.52:21: Now as for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it, and its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow.
verses.52:22: And a bronze capital was upon it, and the height of the one capital was five cubits, with latticework and pomegranates upon the capital all around, all of bronze; and the second pillar had the same, with pomegranates.
verses.52:23: There were ninety-six pomegranates on the outside; all the pomegranates upon the latticework all around were one hundred.
verses.52:24: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.
verses.52:25: And from the city he took one officer who was overseer over the men of war, and seven men from those who saw the king's face who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
verses.52:26: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.52:27: Then the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah went into exile from its land.
verses.52:31: Now it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of the prison house.
verses.52:32: And he spoke kindly with him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.52:33: And he changed his prison garments, and he ate bread before him continually all the days of his life.
verses.52:34: And as for his allowance, a continual allowance was given to him from the king of Babylon, each day's portion, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

notes.1:5: Ketiv reads אצורך while qere reads אֶצָּרְךָ, Qal imperfect 1cs of יָצַר ("shape, form") with an assimilated yod and 2ms suffix.
notes.1:11: Hebrew plays on the sound of שָׁקֵד ("almond tree") here and שֹׁקֵד (Qal active participle of שָׁקַד, "keeping watch") in 1:12.
notes.1:13: סִיר נָפוּחַ is literally "a pot blown upon" (Qal passive participle of נָפַח), meaning fanned by fire and boiling; וּפָנָיו מִפְּנֵי צָפוֹנָה ("and its face is away from the north") pictures the pot tilted southward toward Judah.
notes.1:17: Repeats the root חָתַת ("be shattered/terrified"): תֵּחַת paired with the causative Hiphil אֲחִתְּךָ ("terrify/shatter").
notes.2:15: Ketiv reads 3fs נצתה while qere reads 3cp נִצְּתוּ (Niphal perfect of יָצַת, "be burned"), agreeing in number with plural עָרָיו ("his cities").
notes.2:16: Noph is the Hebrew name for Egyptian Memphis, and qere תַחְפַּנְחֵס (ketiv תחפנס) is Tahpanhes; יִרְעוּךְ is Qal imperfect of רָעָה ("graze"), used figuratively for stripping bare the scalp.
notes.2:20: Ketiv reads אעבוד ("I will not serve"), whereas qere reads אֶעֱבוֹר ("I will not transgress," translated here); MT points שָׁבַרְתִּי and נִתַּקְתִּי as 1cs ("I broke... I snapped"), though some read them as archaic 2fs forms ("you broke... you snapped").
notes.2:27: Ketiv reads ילדתני ("you gave birth to me"), while qere reads יְלִדְתָּנוּ ("you gave birth to us," translated here, matching "save us" at the end of the verse).
notes.2:33: Ketiv reads למדתי (archaic 2fs ending), while qere reads standard Piel perfect 2fs לִמַּדְתְּ ("you have taught"); הָרָעוֹת may denote either "wicked women" (as translated) or "wicked deeds."
notes.2:34: מְצָאתִים can be parsed as 2fs ("you caught/found them," since 2fs perfect takes -tî- before suffixes) or 1cs ("I found them"); כִּי עַל־כׇּל־אֵלֶּה (lit. "indeed upon all these") is syntactically terse and leads into 2:35.
notes.3:1: The Hebrew opens abruptly with the Qal infinitive construct le'mor ("saying"), introducing the divine speech continuing from chapter 2. At the end of the verse, the Qal infinitive absolute shov ("return") can be read either as an incredulous question ("and would you return to Me?") or as an imperative ("yet return to Me!").
notes.3:2: Following the Qere shukkavt ("you have been lain with," Pual of shakhav); the Ketiv uses a coarser Pual form of the verb shagal ("be violated" or "ravished").
notes.3:9: The Hebrew miqqol derives from the root qll ("lightness," i.e., treating her prostitution lightly or casually), though it is spelled identically to a defective form of qol ("voice" or "rumor").
notes.3:12: "Look angrily on you" renders the Hiphil idiom 'appil panay bakhem (lit. "cause My face to fall against you," denoting a frown of displeasure).
notes.3:19: Following the Qere feminine singular verbs tiqre'i ("you would call") and tashuvi ("you would turn away"), matching the feminine singular suffixes earlier in the verse; the Ketiv has masculine plural verbs (tiqre'u and tashuvu).
notes.4:5: Following the Qere tiq'u ("Blow," omitting the conjunction) so that the imperative begins the quoted proclamation; the Ketiv reads we-tiq'u ("and blow").
notes.4:10: "To the throat" renders 'ad-hannefesh; Hebrew nefesh can mean both "throat/neck" and "life/soul," here conveying mortal danger.
notes.4:16: "Besiegers" translates notsrim (Qal participle of natsar, lit. "watchers"), referring to enemy troops keeping siege watch around a city and paralleling "watchmen of a field" in 4:17.
notes.4:19: Following the Qere 'ohilah ("I writhe in pain," Ketiv 'ahulah) and the Qere 2fs verb shama'at ("you have heard," addressing "my soul"); the Ketiv sham'ti preserves either an archaic 2fs ending or a 1cs form ("I have heard").
notes.4:30: Following the Qere we'att ("and you," standard 2fs pronoun; the Ketiv we'atti preserves an archaic 2fs form). The masculine singular Qal passive participle shadud ("devastated one") stands in unusual gender apposition to the feminine singular pronoun.
notes.5:7: The Qere reads 'eslach (standard Qal imperfect of salach, "forgive"), while the Ketiv spells it 'slwch. The Hithpolel verb yitgodadu (from gadad II, "band together") means "throng in troops."
notes.5:8: The Pual participle meyuzzanim ("well-fed," from zun) and the hapax legomenon mashkim ("lusty" or "roaming") are both rare terms describing the horses' unrestrained appetite.
notes.5:17: The second verb (yo'kelu, "they will devour") shifts to the plural, referring to the enemy troops; alternatively, the clause may be read as an asyndetic relative modifying "harvest and bread" ("which your sons and daughters were to eat").
notes.5:24: The Qere reads yoreh ("early rain") without the conjunction, whereas the Ketiv has wyrh ("and early rain").
notes.5:26: The phrase yashur keshak yequshim literally reads "he watches like the crouching of fowlers," using the Qal infinitive construct shak (from shakak, "stoop/crouch") with a distributive singular verb.
notes.6:2: The Qal perfect damiti comes from damah II ("cut off, destroy"; cf. Hos 4:5), rather than damah I ("liken," which is normally Piel when transitive).
notes.6:7: The Qere reads bayir (a rare variant of bor, "well/cistern," which is the Ketiv). The Hiphil forms haqir and heqerah derive from qur/qarar ("keep cool/fresh," or "cause to well up").
notes.6:21: The Qere reads we'avadu (Qal waw-consecutive perfect, "and they will perish"), linking "neighbor and his companion" with the preceding clause; the Ketiv has the imperfect yo'vedu ("will perish") without the conjunction.
notes.6:25: The Qere uses masculine plural forms (tetse'u, teleku) addressing the people as a whole, while the Ketiv has feminine singular forms (tetse'i, teleki) addressing personified Zion.
notes.6:29: The Qere divides the Ketiv's single word (m'shtm, perhaps "from their fire") into two words, me'esh tam ("by the fire [the lead] is consumed"). The opening verb nachar may be parsed as Niphal of charar ("is scorched") or Qal of nachar ("blows fiercely").
notes.7:4: The closing pronoun hemma is masculine plural ("these"), pointing either to the buildings and courts of the temple complex or to the repeated slogan itself.
notes.7:13: The phrase "rising early and speaking" renders the Hiphil infinitive absolute of shakam ("rise early") paired with daber ("speak"), a Hebrew idiom for persistent, earnest action (compare 7:25).
notes.7:18: The Masoretic Text vocalizes the title "queen of heaven" as melekhet rather than malkat ("queen"), resembling the word for "workmanship" and likely reflecting a deliberate vocalic alteration to avoid honoring a pagan deity.
notes.7:22: Following the Qere (read form) hotsi'i ("I brought out," Hiphil infinitive construct with first-person singular suffix); the Ketiv (written form) hotsi lacks the suffix ("bringing out").
notes.7:29: The Hebrew noun nezer denotes consecration or a crown, here referring to uncut hair worn as a sign of consecration and shaved off in mourning.
notes.8:1: Following the Qere (read form) yotsi'u ("they will bring out," Hiphil imperfect without a prefixed conjunction); the Ketiv (written form) includes a prefixed waw ("and they will bring out").
notes.8:6: Following the Qere (read form) bimerutsatam (singular "into their course"); the Ketiv (written form) reads the plural ("into their courses").
notes.8:7: Following the Qere (read form) vesis ("and the swift"); the Ketiv (written form) reads vesus, an alternate spelling of the bird's name that is homographic with the word for "horse" (compare Isaiah 38:14).
notes.8:13: The opening words asof asifem pair the Qal infinitive absolute of asaf ("gather") with the Hiphil imperfect of suf ("bring to an end / sweep away"). The terse closing clause literally reads "and I gave to them, they will pass away from them," understood elliptically as "what I gave them will pass away from them."
notes.8:18: The opening word mabligiti is a unique Masoretic noun derived from the root balag ("brighten / find relief") with a first-person singular suffix, literally "my relief over sorrow," expressing a desperate search for comfort.
notes.9:3: The Hebrew Qal infinitive absolute plus imperfect ("surely supplants") forms a wordplay on the name Jacob (cf. Gen 27:36).
notes.9:7: Qere reads the Qal passive participle "sharpened" (or "beaten/drawn," cf. 1 Kgs 10:16); Ketiv reads the Qal active participle "slaughtering" (i.e., "deadly").
notes.9:18: The indefinite plural Hiphil verb ("they have cast down our dwellings") is also sometimes construed with "our dwellings" as subject ("our dwellings have cast us out").
notes.9:24: Literally "every circumcised one in uncircumcision," referring to those physically circumcised yet uncircumcised in heart (v. 25).
notes.10:5: Literally "like a post/palm-pillar in a cucumber patch," widely understood as a scarecrow (though the noun is also a homonym for "turned/hammered work").
notes.10:11: This verse is the only passage in Jeremiah written in Biblical Aramaic; it preserves both the archaic spelling arqa and the standard Aramaic spelling ar'a for "the earth."
notes.10:13: Qere adds the definite article ("the earth"), whereas Ketiv reads "earth" without the article. The opening phrase literally reads "at the sound of His giving," an idiomatic expression for uttering His voice in thunder.
notes.10:17: Qere reads the standard Qal feminine singular participle ("you who dwell"), replacing the archaic Ketiv feminine ending with hireq compaginis. The noun rendered "bundle" is a hapax legomenon denoting packed belongings or wares.
notes.10:18: The Masoretic Qal imperfect literally reads "so that they may find," without an explicit object, idiomatically meaning "so that they may feel/experience it."
notes.11:2: The Hebrew uses second-person plural verbs ("Hear... and speak") in v. 2 before shifting to second-person singular ("And you shall say") in v. 3.
notes.11:15: The Masoretic Hebrew is notoriously compressed: a poetic feminine singular noun ("vile scheme") stands next to masculine plural "many," "consecrated flesh" takes a Qal plural verb ("passes away"), and "your evil" preserves an archaic second-person feminine singular suffix.
notes.11:19: Literally "the tree with its bread," an idiom for a tree together with its fruit.
notes.11:20: In Hebrew idiom, the "kidneys" and "heart" denote the deepest seat of human emotions, conscience, and inner motives.
